annotation.kind: source selection, tier label, and exact finite-certificate strengthening of Theorem 4.1

assumptions: Numerator and denominator term errors satisfy separate componentwise relative bounds with nonnegative radii.
The exact numerator and denominator are nonzero.
The denominator radius times its condition number is strictly less than one.

conditions.L: The identical fixed statement and P13 shared files are present; the frozen NumStability library is also present.
conditions.N: The fixed statement and P13 shared files are present; no NumStability artifact is present.

formal_statement.lean_header: theorem p13_t3_barycentric_forward_bound {n : Nat} (coeff f deltaNum deltaDen : Fin n -> Real) (epsilonNum epsilonDen : Real) ... : relativeError computed exact <= (epsilonNum*condNum + epsilonDen*condDen)/(1-epsilonDen*condDen)
formal_statement.plain_language: Separately bounded componentwise errors in the barycentric numerator and denominator give an exact forward-error bound with Higham's two condition-number terms and a finite denominator-safety correction.

informal_proof: Apply the generic summation perturbation theorem to the numerator and denominator, use reverse triangle inequality to lower-bound the computed denominator, expand the quotient difference exactly, and combine the two cancellation terms.
informal_statement: Exact finite-certificate counterpart of Theorem 4.1, equations (4.2)-(4.3), based on the perturbed quotient displayed immediately before the theorem.

review_record_not_for_run_prompt.note: The mounted object bounds one perturbed finite sum. No mounted theorem composes two such bounds through a quotient, establishes computed-denominator safety, or proves the exact finite correction corresponding to Theorem 4.1's O(u^2) term.

source_locations.anchor: exact perturbed numerator/denominator expression preceding Theorem 4.1

tier_rationale: The mounted library supplies only the two independent finite-sum perturbation estimates. The proof newly composes them through the barycentric quotient, proves the computed denominator remains nonzero, and derives the exact finite correction whose first-order form is Theorem 4.1.
